name: Paired siblings 2003: stimulus person, six counter-clockwise patterns
origin: Persinger, Koren & Tsang 2003 (Laurentian University), circumcerebral "Octopus" ring; pattern table from the follow-up with strangers (Persinger, Tsang, Booth & Koren 2008)
summary: The helmet program for the stimulus person in Persinger's paired-sibling study: six circumcerebral patterns of 5 min each, rotated counter-clockwise, while this person imagines being with the partner, who sits unexposed with EEG in another room. Persinger's lab reported more 5-6 Hz EEG power in the partner during one of the patterns (four sibling pairs).
notes: Only the stimulus person wears the helmet; the partner (response person) wears EEG electrodes, blindfolded, 5 or 10 m away in another room. The 2003 abstract names the effective pattern "100 msec. with changes in rate of 20 msec." and Persinger & Lavallee 2010 call it "20+2"; both match rows of the lab's six-pattern battery. The table used here is Table 1 of Persinger, Tsang, Booth & Koren 2008, whose stranger pairs went through the sibling study's procedures (Persinger & Lavallee 2010). The project could not open that paper, so the table comes secondhand and is unverified; the verified Table 1 of the Swann paper (persinger-swann-2002-table1) differs in BF2's 1-ms gap, FM2's 1-ms points and FM1's sign (+2 there, while this table reportedly prints -2). This program plays the table in its order, 5 min each (in 2008 half the stimulus persons got the reverse order): BF1 1 ms / 1 ms / 20 ms / +2, BF2 1 / 2 / 100 / +20, BF3 3 / 3000 / 200 / -2, FM1 1 / 1 / 20 / -2, FM2 2 / 1 / 100 / +20, FM3 3 / 3000 / 200 / -2 (point duration / gap between pattern repeats / time on coil 1 / change per coil). FM1 is played as printed. The signs are read literally, + longer and - shorter at each next coil: BF1 runs 20 to 34 ms, the +20 rows 100 to 240 ms, the 200-ms rows 200 to 186 ms and FM1 20 to 6 ms, which is what the same paper's results ("20 msec (+2 msec)") mean in the lab's later notation. Persinger & Lavallee 2010 use "+" to mean shorter, which would give 20 to 6 ms for BF1, 20 to 34 ms for FM1 and 200 to 214 ms for the 200-ms rows; the literal reading was chosen because the +20 rows cannot shorten seven times from 100 ms, Cook 1999's full turns of about 200 to 2000 ms fit it better (216 ms per turn at 20 to 34 ms, 104 ms at 20 to 6 ms), and the Koren software patent (US 6,312,376) uses the plain sign. The schedule the lab actually ran was never published. Ring: eight coils 45 degrees apart on the 10% line, coil 1 over the left frontal region, coil 2 at the left fronto-temporal junction and coil 8 over the right prefrontal region, counter-clockwise seen from above (Persinger & Lavallee 2010): Fp1, FT7, TP7, O1, O2, TP8, FT8, Fp2, an inference since the lab names no electrode sites. The Thomas (frequency-modulated) pulse plays from its exact 849-point table; the burst-firing point values were never published, so the built-in accelerating burst stands in (230 points, 6 -> 30 Hz at 3 ms per point and three times faster at 1 ms). Intensity "1 microTesla range" (2003). As reported: in the siblings, 5.0-6.0 Hz power rose over the partner's frontal and occipital lobes during one pattern (the 2010 retelling says right parietal, with left-sided sensed presences); in four pairs of strangers who had first met for 1 h twice a week for 4 weeks, theta rose mainly over the partners' temporal lobes, slightly more on the right, with the 20+2 field, and the partners reported sensed presences, anger and sexual arousal (2008, as retold by Persinger & Lavallee 2010). Four pairs per study, no sham condition described, no documented blinding of the field schedule, and the papers disagree on which pattern and which lobes: treat it as an unreplicated psi claim. It plays the same six fields as persinger-six-config-battery-2008 (one person, 5 uT) and differs from telepathy-sender (a reconstruction after Murphy's Shiva sessions). Both partners must know about and agree to the experiment; stop if either becomes distressed. Independent double-blind tests of God-Helmet-type fields found no field effect (Granqvist 2005; Gendle & McGrath 2012). Not for people with epilepsy or a seizure history; stop on headache, nausea or distress.
setting: Stimulus person: seated, eyes closed or blindfolded, in a closed, quiet room (the lab used a Faraday cage), imagining being in the other room with the partner and touching him or her. Partner: blindfolded in another room 5 or 10 m away, with 8-channel EEG over the frontal, temporal, parietal and occipital lobes (for example F7, F8, T7, T8, P3, P4, O1, O2); a 20-s baseline, then a 20-s sample during each pattern, scored by someone who does not know which pattern ran.
schedule: Siblings: two sessions a week apart. Strangers (2008): first meet for 1 h twice a week for 4 weeks.
